traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria for 024.0-DEV-IGNORE-INLINE-CODE-REFS are satisfied.
The implementation centralizes inline-code filtering in normalizeCommentLine within src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-format-internal.ts, using a backtick-span regex (/`[^`]*`/g) and replacing each match with spaces of equal length to preserve character/word boundaries. After filtering, annotation detection for @story, @req, and @supports proceeds on the sanitized line, fulfilling REQ-IGNORE-INLINE-CODE, REQ-PRESERVE-BOUNDARIES, and REQ-CENTRALIZED-FILTER.
The dedicated test suite tests/rules/valid-annotation-format-internal.test.ts directly references this story and its requirements. It covers ignoring backtick-wrapped @story and @req, common documentation patterns like "`@story` + `@req`", detection of real annotations outside backticks, multiple backtick spans on a single line, and ensuring lines without backticks are unchanged except for existing normalization. This ensures that documentation-only inline code references do not trigger validation, while real annotations still do. Because normalizeCommentLine is applied per comment line, the same behavior holds for any line within multi-line comments, meeting the multi-line support intent.
The behavior is documented in the JSDoc comments on normalizeCommentLine, which explicitly mention stripping backtick-wrapped inline code spans and preserving character positions. Finally, the full Jest test suite passes, demonstrating no regressions caused by this change. Therefore, the story is fully implemented and validated.
